name: Nordson
headline: Its precision dispensing equipment has held high returns for seventeen years, through a recession and inflation.
what_it_does: Nordson makes equipment, components and spare parts that dispense and control adhesives, coatings, polymers and fluids, along with test and inspection equipment for electronics and single-use medical components. It sells mainly direct in more than 35 countries, 67% of its sales are outside the United States, and no customer is 10% of sales. Its largest part is industrial adhesive dispensing for packaging and product assembly.
why_it_passed: The deciding part, industrial adhesive dispensing, kept its position across a seventeen-year segment record that includes the 2009 recession and the inflation of 2021 to 2023.
Its rivals also earn high returns, so this is not an ordinary field, and the threats the filings name (Asian copies, a well-funded rival) are not shown to be filling the moat.
The core business needs little capital: capital spending was $34.6 million to $64.4 million a year against depreciation of $49.1 million to $71.3 million.
The accounts are clean, bad quarters are reported as bad, and guidance is cut when missed.
why_not_now: At $328.17 a share against a value range of $151.16 to $248.42, the price is above the top. A buyer would earn less than the framework requires, and the 30-year US Treasury pays 5.60%. The price needs the acquired growth to come free.
watch: Most of its growth was bought: organic sales changed +10.8% in FY2022, then -1.4%, -2.5% and -2.5%, under 1% a year compounded.
The capital added through acquisitions (about 957 million euros for ARAG and $790 million for Atrion) earns about 8% after tax, far below the core's return.
Its buybacks name no price and were made above the analysis's value range, and the filings do not say how much of sales comes from parts and consumables.
